claim: test_plan_command.md enumerates scenarios S1-S12 and E1-E5 as the plan command's test obligation, and the sibling test leaves (test_changeset_builder.md, test_classification.md, test_bead_matching.md) enumerate the rest of the module's. Between them they are read as the module's complete test contract — plan/ implements every scenario they name, and the gates are green.
authoritative_source: The enumerations are incomplete against contracts the arch leaves already declare. Two cases are undecided rather than merely uncovered. (1) arch_plan_command.md's "Exit Codes" section owes exit 1 for "malformed JSON" and states "Failure modes never write a partial changeset", but no scenario in test_plan_command.md feeds the command a malformed or zero-length diff document. (2) No leaf under spec/plan/ states the tombstone rule at all: that a fold entry marked removed must be excluded from the pairings handed to NodeMatcher, and from the lookup Resolver reads for epic and parent resolution. Grep for `tombstone`, `removed entr`, `Removed` across arch_plan_command.md, arch_node_matcher.md and test_plan_command.md returns nothing. The rule exists only as a Go doc comment at cmd/spex/plan.go:284-287 and 299-303.
evidence: The gap was surfaced by an independent review of the impact/emit deletion (commit e2157cb), which mutation-tested each behavior against the full suite and confirmed the suite stays green under each mutation; a control mutation failed loudly, so the harness was validated. For (1): deleting `impact`'s TestFR4_ParseDiffJSON_InvalidType, _InvalidImpact, TestE4_DiffFileMalformedJSON and TestE5_DiffFileEmpty dropped parseDiffJSON from 100% to 76.9% coverage while arch_plan_command.md still declares the exit-1 contract, because test_plan_command.md never asked for those scenarios. Four replacement tests are ported in this PR (cmd/spex/helpers_test.go, cmd/spex/plan_test.go) and mutation-verified, so the code is covered again — but they pin a contract the test leaf does not enumerate, which is the defect being reported. For (2): with the `e.Removed` disjunct dropped from planPairingsForMatching (cmd/spex/plan.go:291), a node removed in a prior epic and re-added under the same name matches its own tombstone, and `spex plan` emits a close against an already-closed task plus a successor create carrying old_bead_id instead of a clean create. With the `continue` dropped from newPlanFold (cmd/spex/plan.go:313-316), a removed epic tombstone lands in lookup, ResolveEpicAction skips the epic create, and every op is parented at a dead task id — the PR #217 regression. Both mutations pass the suite. Those lines were already zero-covered before e2157cb; what the deletion removed is the last test in the repository exercising the equivalent rule anywhere, and no leaf states the rule for a future implementer to restore it from. The same review found further behaviors in surviving plan/ code that no scenario pins, each mutation-confirmed green: the `ref:op` wire shape (plan/types.go:97-102 — renaming the tag to `opid` passes, though scripts/apply-br.sh:158 reads `.op_id` and would resolve every in-batch dep to null); ResolvePriority skipping one broken implements entry while honoring valid siblings (plan/resolver.go:133-147); matched-path NodeType propagation and nodeName's data_flow/test_section arms (plan/action_classifier.go:376, 393, 206-216); multiple pairings per spec node (plan/node_matcher.go:96-99); closeOpIDs predicting ids as len(ordered)+len(retargets)+i+1 in a batch mixing a cleanup and a retarget (plan/builder.go:88-91); printing every diff error rather than the first (cmd/spex/plan.go:68-71); and E5_LargeDiffPerformance building its fixture with no requires_module and no uses edges (cmd/spex/plan_test.go:968), so it times an empty dep walk instead of the quadratic collectDeps site at plan/action_classifier.go:239-284 that the retired TestFR3_E4_ClassifyActionsLargeActionList deliberately exercised.
proposed_fix: Decide the two undecided cases and enumerate them. In arch_plan_command.md or arch_node_matcher.md, state the tombstone rule as a contract: a fold entry marked removed is excluded both from the pairings handed to NodeMatcher and from the lookup Resolver reads, and say why (a re-added node must not match its own tombstone; a removed epic must not parent a live op). In test_plan_command.md, add the scenarios that pin it, plus the malformed-diff and zero-length-diff scenarios the Exit Codes section already owes. Then triage the remaining behaviors above: each is either a scenario a test leaf should name, or a property no contract claims — decide which, per item, rather than in bulk. collectDeps's cost is a performance property, not a contract, and may well be rejected on that basis. Whatever the corrections owe is minted in the normal way; no beads are filed by hand for any of this.
